Hi Samira — looping in some practical steps to get a local testbed running. I kept this to a smoke-test level so your engs can validate integration feasibility in a day.

Quickstart checklist (local smoke test):
- Prereqs: Docker (20xx+), Node 18+, Python 3.11, git, curl
- Clone: git clone https://github.com/redwood-inference/devonramp-quickstart.git
- Unpack: unzip devonramp_quickstart.zip (contains two folders: python-sample and ts-sample plus sample_docs/)

Python sample (python-sample):
- Create venv: python -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate
- Install: pip install -r requirements.txt (fastapi, httpx, redwood-sdk==0.2.1)
- Env vars (example):
  - REDWOOD_API_KEY="<sandbox-key>"
  - REDWOOD_API_HOST=https://api.redwood-inference.com
  - REDWOOD_CACHE_DIR=./kvcache
- Run: uvicorn app.main:app --reload --port 8001
- Test embedding flow: POST /embed with sample_docs/ -> returns vectors; run reranker script to validate top-k ordering
- Tool calling demo: POST /call-tool -> hits a local stub (db_lookup) and returns structured JSON with tool metadata (see sample tool module)

TypeScript sample (ts-sample):
- Install: cd ts-sample && npm ci
- Env: create .env with the same REDWOOD_* vars, plus NODE_TLS_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED=0 for local self-signed certs if you use Docker compose
- Run: npm run dev (starts a tiny Next.js app + API route that shows streaming responses + function/tool calling example)

Auth guidance (short):
- Sandbox: easiest for pilots is API keys scoped to the sandbox project (rotate keys, short TTL). For internal production apps recommend mTLS + short-lived tokens via our OAuth bridge.
- Routing: configure a fallback policy: primary (large open model), fallback to quantized small model for cost-sensitive endpoints. We can push routing rules via the deployment config in the repo.

Embedding/reranker notes:
- At ~10k docs we recommend: 1) batched embed requests (batch size 64–128 depending on seq length), 2) float16 quantization for production (saves cost with minimal quality drop), 3) monitor recall vs latency with the provided eval harness.
- The quickstart includes a basic reranker that uses a small cross-encoder and an L2 distance rerank baseline; switch to cross-encoder only for narrow clinical queries.

Attachments included in the zip: minimal Dockerfile, sample prompt templates, tiny sample docs (4–6 clinical notes) and a runbook.md with the exact commands above.

If you want, Ben can stand up a short recording we can share showing a full run-through.
